headline_en: Bangladesh condemns Israeli attacks in Lebanon and the killing of Dipali
summary_en: Bangladesh's foreign ministry condemned recent Israeli attacks in Lebanon and the death of Bangladeshi woman worker Dipali Begum, killed in an Israeli air strike on her employer's house in Hamra, Beirut. The embassy in Lebanon is in touch with her family and will arrange to bring the body home when the situation allows.

facts.statement: Bangladeshi woman worker Dipali Begum was killed when Israeli forces carried out an air strike on the house of her employer (kafil) in the Hamra area of Beirut, Lebanon; the building collapsed. Seven people in total died in the strike, including her employer and members of his family.

Bangladesh's foreign ministry issued a press release on Friday 10 April 2026 (published on X on 11 April) condemning civilian casualties from Israel's recent attacks in Lebanon and the killing of Bangladeshi citizen Dipali Begum in Beirut, saying the attacks disrupt ongoing efforts for peace and stability in the region.

The foreign ministry said the Bangladesh embassy in Lebanon is in contact with Dipali Begum's family and will arrange to bring her body back to Bangladesh when the situation becomes favourable. The government expressed condolences and said it would stand by the family.
A foreign ministry official confirmed to Prothom Alo on 10 April 2026 the death of Bangladeshi woman worker Dipali Begum in an Israeli air strike in Beirut, the capital of Lebanon.

Dipali Begum, daughter of Sheikh Mofazzal of Purba Shalepur Munshirchar village, Char Harirampur union, Charbhadrasan upazila, Faridpur, was the fourth of two brothers and three sisters and had gone to Lebanon two years before her death (April 2026) to relieve her family's poverty.

people_cases.who: Dipali Begum, daughter of Sheikh Mofazzal, Purba Shalepur Munshirchar village, Char Harirampur union, Charbhadrasan, Faridpur
people_cases.what_happened: Went to Lebanon two years earlier as a worker; killed on Wednesday 8 April 2026 evening when an Israeli air strike collapsed her employer's house in Hamra, Beirut; seven died including the employer and family members.
people_cases.outcome: Dead; embassy in contact with family, body to be repatriated when the situation allows.

headline_en: 'Bring my husband's body back, I want to see him one last time'
summary_en: Shah Alam Bhuiyan (45) of Jiruin village, Brahmanpara, Cumilla, was killed on 1 April 2026 near Dubai when debris from a drone used in the ongoing Middle East war fell on him as he walked to work at a farm. His family, living in a dilapidated tin house after his 27 years abroad, is demanding that the government bring the body home quickly; the UNO visited and promised support.

facts.date: Wednesday 1 April 2026, about 6 am local time
facts.statement: Bangladeshi worker Shah Alam Bhuiyan (45), from Jiruin village, Sahebabad union, Brahmanpara upazila, Cumilla, died on the spot when the debris of a drone used in the ongoing Middle East war fell on him while he was walking to work at a farm near Dubai. A co-worker walking about 10 cubits behind him fainted at the sight; the country's police came and recovered the body.
A related Prothom Alo headline cited at the end of the article describes the incident as 'One Bangladeshi killed in Iran's drone attack in the Arab Emirates'.
Shah Alam Bhuiyan, who worked on a farm near Dubai, earned a salary of 30-35 thousand taka and sent 20-25 thousand taka home for household expenses, according to his wife Nayna Akter.

Shah Alam Bhuiyan spent 27 years abroad: about eight years in Oman, then, after returning to Bangladesh, about 18 years in Dubai. Despite this his home is a broken four-roofed tin house and relatives say he never managed to prosper.
facts.source_in_article: Fazlur Rahman Bhuiyan, cousin (Oman-based migrant); reporter's observation

facts.statement: The family of Shah Alam Bhuiyan (wife Nayna Akter, eldest daughter Sharmin Akter, cousin Fazlur Rahman Bhuiyan) demanded that the government bring his body back from the UAE quickly.

Brahmanpara UNO Mahmuda Jahan visited the family in Jiruin village, promised that the upazila administration would try to stand by the family, said the relatives' demand for quick repatriation of the body had been reported to higher authorities, and hoped the body would be brought back soon through the relevant ministry.
The wife learned of the death at about 11 am on Wednesday 1 April 2026; her last phone call with her husband was around noon on Tuesday 31 March and lasted about an hour.

Cousin Habibur Rahman Bhuiyan, who two years earlier spent three months at the same Dubai workplace, said he spoke by phone to the co-worker who was behind Shah Alam; the co-worker was brushing his teeth on the way to work when the debris fell and Shah Alam died instantly.

people_cases.who: Shah Alam Bhuiyan, 45, Jiruin village, Sahebabad union, Brahmanpara, Cumilla
people_cases.destination: United Arab Emirates (farm near Dubai); earlier Oman
people_cases.what_happened: 27 years abroad (about 8 in Oman, 18 in Dubai), earning 30-35 thousand taka. Killed on 1 April 2026 about 6 am when drone debris fell on him on the way to work.
people_cases.outcome: Dead; leaves wife Nayna Akter, two married daughters (Sharmin, Mim Akter) and two sons (Shakil 12, Minhaj 7). Family demanding repatriation of the body; UNO promised support.

headline_en: USD 2 billion loan being considered to protect the balance of payments
summary_en: At a 29 March 2026 meeting with senior business journalists, Bangladesh Bank governor Md. Mostakur Rahman said Bangladesh is at a very early stage of planning to seek USD 2 billion from the IMF and other lenders for balance-of-payments support amid the Middle East situation. Journalists warned of a hit to remittances and overseas jobs; central bank officials said the near-term risk to remittances is low but a prolonged war could hurt remittances and migrants' employment.

facts.statement: Bangladesh Bank governor Md. Mostakur Rahman said Bangladesh is planning, if needed, to take USD 2 billion in foreign assistance from the IMF and other global lenders to protect the balance of payments under pressure from domestic problems and the Middle East situation; the matter is at a very early stage, talks have been held with the IMF, and the Economic Relations Division (ERD) is trying other sources.

Journalists at the Bangladesh Bank meeting warned that the Middle East crisis could have a large negative effect on remittances and overseas employment, and advised raising the remittance incentive and taking special support measures for migrants if they are forced to return home.
facts.source_in_article: Senior business journalists at the meeting

facts.statement: Bangladesh Bank's top officials said the risk of a negative effect on remittances is low for now because, as several deputy governors said, in such situations migrants send all their savings home; but if the war is prolonged it could hurt remittances and migrants' employment.
The meeting was told that remittances at the end of the current fiscal year could be USD 2 to 2.5 billion higher than in the previous fiscal year.
Bangladesh Bank said foreign-exchange reserves are currently at a comfortable level and it is watchful that no instability arises in the foreign-exchange market.
Among recommendations journalists raised at the Bangladesh Bank meeting was increasing the dollar quota limit for foreign travel.

named_actors.name: Md. Mostakur Rahman
named_actors.what_the_article_says: Governor of Bangladesh Bank; chaired the 29 March 2026 meeting and disclosed the USD 2 billion balance-of-payments assistance plan.

headline_en: More than USD 3 billion in remittances in 24 days; a new record possible
summary_en: Bangladesh Bank reported that migrants sent USD 3.05 billion in the first 24 days of March 2026, an Eid month, so March could set a new single-month record. July to 24 March FY2025-26 remittances were USD 25.504 billion, up 10.90 percent year on year. The Middle East crisis has pushed up the dollar price for remittances, and eight economists advised the central bank to hold on to reserves.

facts.statement: Bangladeshi migrants sent USD 3.05 billion (305 crore dollars) home in the first 24 days of March 2026, the month of Eid-ul-Fitr; March could set a new single-month remittance record.
The highest monthly remittance in Bangladesh's history was in March 2025: USD 3,295.63 million (329 crore 56 lakh 30 thousand dollars).
The second-highest monthly remittance was December 2025 at USD 3,226.6 million (322 crore 66 lakh dollars) and the third-highest January 2026 at USD 3.17 billion (317 crore dollars).

From July to 24 March of fiscal year 2025-26 Bangladesh received USD 25,504 million (2,550 crore 40 lakh dollars) in remittances, 10.90 percent more than the USD 21,238 million (2,123 crore 80 lakh dollars) in the same period of the previous fiscal year.

Because of the Middle East crisis the dollar price paid for remittances has gone up; eight leading economists, in a recent meeting with Bangladesh Bank, advised it to hold on to reserves, not to cut the policy rate yet, and to arrange alternative energy sources to the Middle East.

headline_en: Saudi Arabia keen to widen areas of bilateral relations
summary_en: On 22 February 2026 Saudi ambassador Abdullah Zafer H. bin Abiyah paid a courtesy call on foreign minister Khalilur Rahman and expressed interest in widening bilateral ties. He said Saudi Arabia issued 750,000 work visas and 1.4 million visas in total to Bangladeshis in 2025 and that there are more job opportunities for skilled and semi-skilled workers.

facts.statement: Saudi Arabia issued 750,000 (7 lakh 50 thousand) work visas and a total of 1.4 million (14 lakh) visas to Bangladeshi nationals in 2025.
facts.source_in_article: Saudi ambassador Abdullah Zafer H. bin Abiyah, via foreign ministry notice

facts.statement: The Saudi ambassador to Bangladesh said that because of various ongoing development activities in Saudi Arabia there are further employment opportunities there for skilled and semi-skilled workers.
facts.source_in_article: Saudi ambassador Abdullah Zafer H. bin Abiyah, via foreign ministry notice

facts.statement: Foreign minister Khalilur Rahman thanked Saudi Arabia for giving employment to a large number of Bangladeshi workers and pointed to potential for wider cooperation in trade, investment, energy and other priority sectors; the Saudi ambassador expressed support for the current government and a wish to integrate and expand bilateral relations.
The foreign minister said diplomatic relations began with the establishment of the Bangladesh embassy in Saudi Arabia in 1976 under President Ziaur Rahman, who made a visit to Saudi Arabia in 1977.
Earlier the same day the Saudi ambassador also called on state minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed Islam, who praised reforms under Saudi Vision 2030.

named_actors.name: Abdullah Zafer H. bin Abiyah
named_actors.what_the_article_says: Saudi ambassador to Bangladesh; stated the 2025 visa figures and said more jobs exist for skilled and semi-skilled workers.

headline_en: Special government initiative: Saudi-based migrants can come home for 20 thousand taka
summary_en: The interim government announced on 30 January 2026 a special low one-way fare of about BDT 20,000 for migrant workers on the Saudi Arabia-Bangladesh route, using Biman flights that would otherwise fly empty during Hajj. Minimum fares are BDT 20,500 one way and BDT 42,000 return on Madinah/Jeddah-Dhaka, valid for travel to Bangladesh 18 April to 25 May 2026 and back to Saudi Arabia 30 May to 30 June 2026, with 80,000 tickets targeted.

facts.statement: Under a special arrangement for Bangladeshi migrant workers, the minimum one-way fare on the Madinah-Dhaka and Jeddah-Dhaka routes is set at BDT 20,500 (the announcement headline figure is 'only BDT 20,000' one way on the Saudi Arabia-Bangladesh route).
Under the same special arrangement the minimum return-ticket fare on Madinah-Dhaka-Madinah and Jeddah-Dhaka-Jeddah is BDT 42,000.

facts.date: 18 April to 25 May 2026; 30 May to 30 June 2026
facts.statement: The special fare applies for travel to Bangladesh from 18 April to 25 May 2026, and for returning from Bangladesh to Saudi Arabia from 30 May to 30 June 2026.
A target of selling 80,000 tickets in total, in Saudi Arabia and Bangladesh combined, has been set under the special fare arrangement, which is operated by state carrier Biman Bangladesh Airlines.
facts.source_in_article: Sheikh Bashiruddin, adviser, Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism

facts.statement: The adviser explained that during Hajj Biman normally carries passengers one way and many return flights are empty; the scheme uses those empty flights and could bring Biman more than BDT 100 crore in additional income for the first time in its history.
facts.source_in_article: Sheikh Bashiruddin, adviser, Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism

facts.statement: Chief Adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus called the initiative a milestone of migrant-friendly policy but warned that in the past many good initiatives for migrants collapsed after a while for lack of proper monitoring, and said it must be ensured that this one stays 100 percent effective.

named_actors.name: Biman Bangladesh Airlines
named_actors.what_the_article_says: State airline operating the special low fares for migrant workers on Madinah/Jeddah-Dhaka during the 2026 Hajj period.

headline_en: 60,000 drivers to be trained to raise employment and remittances
summary_en: On 13 January 2026 the advisers' council committee on government purchase approved a BDT 231 crore service procurement to train 60,000 drivers (40,000 new, 20,000 existing) through BRTC with BMET's support, under the World Bank-financed Bangladesh Road Safety project. The finance adviser said drivers would be trained on heavy equipment such as cranes and excavators for overseas jobs. The article also covers unrelated purchases.

facts.statement: The government will train 60,000 drivers to create jobs and boost remittances; a BDT 231 crore proposal to buy the training service ('Non-Consultancy Service for Delivery of Commercial Driver Training', a BRTA package under the 'Bangladesh Road Safety' project) was approved by the advisers' council committee on government purchase. The state body Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) will deliver the training.

Of the 60,000 drivers, 40,000 will be entirely new drivers given 80 days of training over 4 months, and 20,000 existing professional drivers will get a 5-day skills-upgrade course. The Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET) will assist, and training, certificates and licences will be given following set rules and standards.
Under the driver training project, 40,000 drivers will have their eyes tested and 20,000 drivers will be given glasses.

Finance adviser Salehuddin Ahmed said that for overseas employment drivers will be trained to operate heavy equipment such as cranes and excavators; that current drivers have no demand abroad; and that after training they will become eligible for high-paid jobs abroad. He said the project is part of a long-term employment strategy and has nothing to do with the election.

The 'Bangladesh Road Safety' project, implemented through the Roads and Highways Department, was approved by ECNEC in 2023 with a term of 1 May 2023 to 30 June 2028, with BDT 1,238 crore from the state treasury and a BDT 3,760 crore World Bank loan; other work under the project is reported to be slow.

headline_en: Five thousand travel agencies will close if the new ordinance takes effect
summary_en: At a 4 January 2026 press conference, former ATAB president S N Manzur Murshed Mahbub and other leaders demanded cancellation of the Travel Agency Registration and Control Ordinance 2026, gazetted on 1 January, saying it would force about 5,000 non-IATA agencies to close. They objected to bans on buying tickets from other agencies and on running a recruiting agency at a travel agency's address, a BDT 10 lakh bank guarantee, and suspension of registration without a hearing.

facts.statement: The gazette of the Travel Agency Registration and Control Ordinance 2026 was published on 1 January 2026. ATAB leaders say it provides that a travel agency cannot buy or sell tickets from another travel agency on the basis of an affidavit.
facts.source_in_article: S N Manzur Murshed Mahbub, former ATAB president, and other ATAB leaders

facts.statement: Bangladesh has about 5,800 registered travel agencies, of which only 800 are members of the International Air Transport Association (IATA); the other roughly 5,000 cannot issue air tickets themselves and buy them from other agencies.

Travel agencies must show an annual sales statement of BDT 50 lakh to renew registration; ATAB leaders say agencies barred from buying tickets from other agencies will be unable to show this and will be forced to close.

The ordinance provides for a bank guarantee of BDT 10 lakh for offline travel agencies; Mohammad Jalal Uddin Tipu said the roughly 5,000 agencies that could not become IATA members for lack of financial capacity cannot possibly provide a BDT 10 lakh security.
facts.source_in_article: Mohammad Jalal Uddin Tipu, convener, ATAB Sadasya Kalyan Oikyajot

facts.statement: The ordinance proposes prohibiting the operation of a recruiting agency business at a travel agency's address. ATAB leaders said recruiting agencies have long run travel agencies at the same address to ease services for outgoing migrant workers, and that compulsory separate offices will raise costs and so increase the per-head expense of migrant workers.

Under a clause of the ordinance the government can temporarily suspend a travel agency's registration certificate without a hearing; ATAB leaders said this risks harassment and financial loss and that an opportunity for self-defence should be given before any decision.

Former ATAB president S N Manzur Murshed Mahbub told a press conference at the National Press Club that about 5,000 travel agencies risk closing if the ordinance takes effect and that the ordinance should be cancelled.

named_actors.name: Association of Travel Agents of Bangladesh (ATAB)
named_actors.what_the_article_says: Its former president S N Manzur Murshed Mahbub and other leaders demanded cancellation of the Travel Agency Registration and Control Ordinance 2026.

headline_en: 1 percent tax now payable on cash remittance transfers from the United States
summary_en: From 1 January 2026 a US federal excise tax of 1 percent applies to remittances sent abroad from the United States by cash, money order, cashier's cheque or similar physical means; transfers from bank accounts, debit cards or digital methods are exempt. Senders and money-transfer operators say it discourages sending and could push people to illegal channels.

facts.statement: From 1 January 2026, sending remittances from the United States to Bangladesh or any other country in cash costs an extra USD 1 in tax per USD 100: a new federal excise tax, formally the 'Excise Tax on Remittance Transfers', imposed under the 'One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025'.

The 1 percent US remittance tax applies only to remittances sent by cash, money order, cashier's cheque or similar physical means. Sending from a bank account, debit card or by digital methods (such as online transfer) carries no extra tax.
facts.source_in_article: The law, as reported; Asim Kumar, money-transfer agent in New York

facts.statement: The bill containing the remittance tax was passed in Congress in May 2025 and signed by President Donald Trump on 4 July 2025.
Experts say the US remittance tax will hit hardest undocumented migrants without bank savings accounts and low-income migrants.

Standard Express chief executive Mohammad Malek said the United States was the top source of remittances to Bangladesh until July 2025 and has now fallen to fifth place; he said the extra tax may encourage many to send money through illegal channels.
facts.source_in_article: Mohammad Malek, chief executive, Standard Express

facts.statement: US-based sender Zohaib Chowdhury said the tax somewhat discourages him from sending money to Bangladesh and that it would help migrants if the Bangladesh government raised the remittance incentive; the article adds that the government and Bangladesh Bank could increase monitoring and raise the incentive to encourage legal channels.
Economists say the US remittance tax will also affect other remittance-dependent countries such as Mexico, India and the Philippines.

named_actors.name: Standard Express
named_actors.what_the_article_says: Money-transfer company whose chief executive Mohammad Malek commented that the tax is US law and must be followed.

headline_en: One billion dollars in remittances arrived in just 8 days
summary_en: Bangladesh received USD 1 billion in remittances from 1 to 8 December 2025, 21 percent more than a year earlier, creating a dollar surplus in banks. Bangladesh Bank bought USD 202 million from 13 commercial banks on 9 December at a cut-off rate of BDT 122.29.

facts.statement: Bangladesh received USD 1 billion (100 crore dollars) in remittances from 1 to 8 December 2025, of which USD 131 million came on 8 December; the same period a year earlier brought USD 831 million, a 21 percent rise.

From July to 8 December 2025 Bangladesh received USD 14.04 billion (1,404 crore dollars) in remittances against USD 11.96 billion (1,196 crore dollars) in the same period a year earlier, a 17 percent rise.

With a dollar surplus in banks, Bangladesh Bank bought USD 202 million (20 crore 20 lakh dollars) from 13 commercial banks through a multiple-price auction; the exchange rate ranged from BDT 122.27 to BDT 122.29 per dollar with a cut-off rate of BDT 122.29.
Bangladesh Bank began buying dollars by auction on 13 July 2025 and has bought USD 2,514 million (251 crore 40 lakh dollars; USD 2.51 billion) so far in fiscal year 2025-26.

headline_en: 'Study Abroad Fair' festive with crowds of those interested in studying abroad
summary_en: Prothom Alo's two-day 'Study Abroad Fair 2025' opened on 24 October 2025 at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in Agargaon, Dhaka, with university representatives and education consultancies advising students on scholarships, admissions and visas. The fair is open 10 am to 8 pm, continues online at www.studyabroadfair.pro until 2 November, and includes panel sessions on studying in the UK, Europe, New Zealand and Australia.

facts.statement: Prothom Alo organised the two-day 'Study Abroad Fair 2025' at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre, Agargaon, Dhaka, on Friday 24 and Saturday 25 October 2025, open to all from 10 am to 8 pm, giving information and advice on higher education abroad, admission processes, scholarships, visas and applications, with panel sessions and special offers from participating organisations.

The Study Abroad Fair 2025 runs online for 10 days, until 2 November 2025, at www.studyabroadfair.pro, where students can enter organisations' online booths, get information and contact representatives directly; there is also an online quiz with prizes.

The fair was presented by the British Council, 'powered by' UCSI University Bangladesh Branch Campus, with Prime Bank as banking partner and the Foreign Admission and Career Development Consultants Association of Bangladesh (FACD-CAB) as strategic partner.
Prime Bank PLC's chief bancassurance officer M M Rabiul Hasan said students going abroad to study need financial support and that Prime Bank will always be there to ensure that support.
facts.source_in_article: M M Rabiul Hasan, Prime Bank PLC

facts.statement: Education consultancies with stalls at the fair included Meises Education Meet (মেইসেস এডুকেশন মিট), Schengen Edu Limited, CHS Education Limited, 10 Minute School, BD Expert Education Consultancy, Education At (এডুকেশন অ্যাট), Maximus Education and Migration, NHP, Universal College Bangladesh, Backbone Limited, Quest Educare and Career Services, Universal Education, Global Vision, Foreign Study Solution, STS Global Education, Edvoy, Haque Consultancy, EduAid Immigration Services and Edu Aimers.

Sessions: on 24 October at 5:30 pm 'Education Consultancy with Google by Aleph' (Ahsanur Rahman) and at 6 pm a 'Study Abroad' panel; on 25 October at 12 noon 'Study in UK and Europe', at 4:30 pm 'IELTS and Study Abroad' by Munzereen Shahid, and at 6 pm 'Study in New Zealand and Australia'.

Prothom Alo managing editor Anisul Hoque said the fair is meant to help students avoid being cheated when going abroad and to get admission to the best institutions; panel speakers advised proper guidance, planning and adequate preparation for going abroad for higher education.

key_quote_bn: মেলায় বিদেশে উচ্চশিক্ষা, ভর্তিপ্রক্রিয়া, স্কলারশিপ, ভিসা ও আবেদনসংক্রান্ত বিভিন্ন তথ্য ও পরামর্শ দেওয়া হচ্ছে

headline_en: 21 more women and children held hostage for trafficking rescued from Teknaf hills
summary_en: A joint Coast Guard and Navy team rescued 21 people, including women and children and mostly Rohingya, who were being held hostage in the deep hills of Baharchhara, Teknaf, to be trafficked to Malaysia by sea; the traffickers fled. The article lists a string of similar rescues and arrests in Teknaf in September 2025 and says 68 traffickers have been arrested and 201 people rescued there so far in 2025.

facts.statement: A joint Coast Guard and Navy team rescued 21 people including women and children who were being held hostage in the deep hills near Karachipara ghat, Baharchhara union, Teknaf, Cox's Bazar, for trafficking to Malaysia by sea. The traffickers fled on sensing the forces; most of those rescued are Rohingya. They were handed to Teknaf police station to be returned to relatives.
facts.source_in_article: Lt Commander Siam-ul-Haque, media officer, Coast Guard headquarters

facts.statement: Earlier operations in Teknaf: on 1 October the Coast Guard rescued eight women and children near Jummapara hill, Baharchhara; on the night of 29 September three people including three brokers (as printed) were recovered from a hill in the same area; on 23 September five abducted people were rescued and two traffickers detained in the Kachchhapia hills; the day before, RAB and BGB arrested three traffickers with weapons and rescued 84 people; on 18 September the Coast Guard rescued 66 people; on 16 September BGB detained 12 traffickers and rescued 11 people.

According to law-enforcement figures, 68 traffickers have been arrested and 201 people rescued from Teknaf so far in 2025. (The article's own list of September operations includes rescues of 84 and 66 people, so the figures do not obviously reconcile.)
The tendency for human trafficking by sea rises in the winter season.

Teknaf Model Thana OC Abu Zayed Md. Nazmun Noor said seven Rohingya women and one child rescued on Wednesday were sent to court, and the 21 women and children rescued on Thursday 2 October would be sent to court on Friday.
facts.source_in_article: Abu Zayed Md. Nazmun Noor, OC Teknaf Model Thana

headline_en: United States sends back 39 Bangladeshis

headline_en: The safest path is to maintain strategic neutrality (interview with security analyst A N M Muniruzzaman)
summary_en: In a long interview on geopolitics, security analyst A N M Muniruzzaman (president, BIPSS) touches on migration in two places: Middle East conflict directly hurts Bangladesh because it is the largest labour market with over 3 million Bangladeshis, and the alleged involvement of Bangladeshi youths in extremist activity in Malaysia threatens the labour market in Malaysia, Singapore and elsewhere unless the home ministry acts visibly. The rest covers Myanmar, India, Rohingya and US tariffs.

facts.statement: Security analyst A N M Muniruzzaman said the Middle East is Bangladesh's largest labour market, with more than 30 lakh (3 million) Bangladeshis working there, and a major source of foreign-currency earnings, so conflict in the Middle East has a direct adverse effect on Bangladesh.
facts.source_in_article: A N M Muniruzzaman, president, Bangladesh Institute of Peace and Security Studies (BIPSS)

facts.statement: Several young Bangladeshis in Malaysia have been accused of involvement in extremist activity; according to Muniruzzaman they were taking steps to collect money there and send it to ISIS in the Middle East, giving the case an international dimension, and they very likely have contacts with extremist groups in Bangladesh.

Muniruzzaman warned that unless Bangladesh takes strong, clear and visible steps regarding those jailed in Malaysia or being sent back over the extremism allegations, the labour market for Bangladeshis will suffer a large negative effect not only in Malaysia but in Singapore and many other countries; he said the home ministry had taken no visible action.
Bangladeshis accused of extremist activity in Malaysia are in jail there or are being sent back to Bangladesh, as referred to in the interview (no numbers given).
Muniruzzaman said human trafficking to various countries is taking place from the Rohingya camps in Bangladesh, alongside drug and small-arms smuggling.

headline_en: Would closing Biman's Tokyo flight be a gain or a loss? (column)
summary_en: Japan-based journalist Monzurul Huq writes that Biman Bangladesh Airlines, which resumed Dhaka-Tokyo flights in September 2023 after 17 years, is suspending the route indefinitely for the third time in the first week of July 2025, citing losses. He describes what the direct flight meant for Bangladeshis in Japan, argues that starting with three weekly flights for a community of just over 20,000 was a mistake, and urges keeping at least one weekly flight.

facts.statement: Biman Bangladesh Airlines' Tokyo flight, restarted in September 2023 after 17 years, is being suspended indefinitely for the third time in the first week of July 2025, according to the columnist; Biman cites financial loss. Twice before, Biman had started and soon stopped Tokyo flights citing losses from too few passengers.
facts.source_in_article: Monzurul Huq, Japan-based journalist and writer (column)

facts.statement: The direct Biman flight took only six to seven hours between Tokyo and Dhaka with no transit, offered some ticket-price advantage, and gave some extra baggage allowance compared with other airlines, according to the columnist who flew it at least three times.

When the Tokyo flight restarted (for the third time), the number of Bangladeshis living in Japan was a little over 20,000 according to Japan's immigration bureau. Nepalis permanently living in Japan now exceed 150,000 (one and a half lakh).
facts.source_in_article: Japan immigration bureau figures cited by Monzurul Huq

facts.statement: Biman started with three flights a week, targeting also Nepalis and people from India's eastern states living in Japan (with a connecting Dhaka-Kathmandu flight); at first most passengers were Nepali, but Biman could not retain Indian and Nepali passengers and cut to two flights a week before the suspension.

A delegation of Bangladeshis living in Japan met interim government head Professor Muhammad Yunus in Tokyo and handed him a memorandum demanding the flight be kept; he promised to look into it, but Biman's decision did not change. Many expatriates have also protested at the Bangladesh embassy.

Passengers who flew the route recently say they did not see empty flights; the columnist says the flight also helped Bangladeshi fresh vegetables, fruit and agricultural products enter the Japanese market, and recommends keeping at least one weekly Tokyo flight.

headline_en: After a year and a half of running around over a duplicate birth registration, he learned what to do
summary_en: People with two online birth registrations are being refused e-passports, NID corrections and their children's birth registration, and spend months finding out that they must apply to cancel one registration at the Office of the Registrar General, Birth and Death Registration. One case is a returnee from Saudi Arabia whose daughter's e-passport application (to join her husband in Libya) was cancelled; a broker demanded BDT 10,000. The article also reports delays in registration since administrators replaced elected representatives.

facts.statement: If a person has two birth registrations online, the passport office cancels the e-passport application: the Uttara passport office cancelled the 2024 e-passport application of Jannatul Akter Priti (18) of Gazipur for this reason.

To fix a duplicate online birth registration, the person must apply for cancellation of one birth registration (described as 'transfer, that is, cancellation', not a 'reset'); the Office of the Registrar General, Birth and Death Registration in Dhaka says that when people with duplicate registrations apply, one is cancelled.
facts.source_in_article: Registrar General Md. Zahid Hossain; applicants

facts.statement: In Md. Selim's case (Mirpur, DNCC ward 6), after he applied for cancellation the Registrar General's office investigates and sends a report to the ward office, which takes about a month; after that he must apply afresh for birth registration. Until his own registration is corrected he cannot register his children's births.

In Shahidul Islam's case (Shibpur, Narsingdi), the family was told the first birth registration must be kept; they then applied on 16 June 2025 to cancel the first registration, submitting his children's education certificates as proof, and were told on 27 June that it had been cancelled, after which the NID could be corrected. NID name correction had been refused in November 2024 because two birth registrations existed online.

When Joynal Abedin tried locally to find out how to resolve his daughter's cancelled e-passport application, nobody told him and a broker demanded BDT 10,000; the passport office later told him to contact the Registrar General's office, where he learned what to do.

How the duplicates arose: Joynal Abedin registered his daughter's birth in 2016 (passport made that year for Umrah travel to Saudi Arabia) and made a second registration in 2021 with different spellings because his name differed in his passport and her education certificates say only 'Jannatul'.

For union parishads, upazilas and municipalities the UNO now gives final approval for birth and death registration certificates; in city corporations the administrative officer of the regional office does, and corrections in cities need the deputy commissioner's approval. Administrative officers say certificates are issued in three to five days unless the application has errors.

Complaints of delay: in Nowhata municipality, Paba, Rajshahi, a digital birth certificate applied for on 15 January 2025 arrived in mid-May, and a death certificate took a month (received 15 May 2025); victims say the UNO comes once a month to sign applications and the police station OC's signature is also required. Paba UNO Arafat Aman Aziz said he signs many certificates at once on a set day and delays are occasional.
facts.source_in_article: Zulfiqar Ali; Abdur Razzak; Arafat Aman Aziz, UNO Paba

facts.statement: On 25 June 2025 more than 30,000 births were registered, more than 20,000 correction applications were settled and more than 3,500 deaths were registered, according to the Registrar General's office website.
facts.source_in_article: Office of the Registrar General website

facts.statement: After the July uprising most union parishad chairmen and city councillors went into hiding and registration stopped in most places for more than two months, until administrators were appointed.

headline_en: Reserves rise to USD 30 billion on remittances and foreign loans
summary_en: Bangladesh Bank's gross reserves reached USD 30.51 billion on 26 June 2025 (USD 25.51 billion under BPM6), helped by higher remittances through legal channels since the fall of the Awami League government and more than USD 5 billion in foreign loans. Remittances in FY2024-25 up to the previous week were USD 29.46 billion against USD 23.91 billion in all of FY2023-24, and the dollar rate banks pay exchange houses eased to BDT 122.70-122.80.

facts.statement: Bangladesh received USD 23.91 billion in remittances in fiscal year 2023-24; in fiscal year 2024-25 up to the week before 27 June 2025 it had received USD 29.46 billion, about USD 6 billion more.

Because dollar supply has increased, the dollar price for remittances has fallen: banks used to buy dollars from overseas exchange houses at more than BDT 123 and now pay BDT 122.70 to BDT 122.80; importers settle at BDT 123-124.

Bankers say remittances through legal channels rose after the fall of the Awami League government in August 2024 because money laundering declined and the interim government's monitoring increased; the central bank has not sold dollars from reserves for 10 months.

Bangladesh Bank's foreign-exchange reserves stood at USD 30.51 billion gross, USD 25.51 billion under the IMF's BPM6 method, and USD 19.80 billion usable; on 31 July 2024 gross reserves were USD 25.92 billion and BPM6 reserves USD 20.48 billion.

Recent inflows added to reserves: USD 1.34 billion from two overdue IMF instalments, USD 500 million from the World Bank and USD 900 million from the ADB; a further USD 900 million from the IMF and USD 1.5 billion from the World Bank, AIIB, Japan and the OPEC Fund were expected within June, taking gross reserves to USD 32 billion by month end.

headline_en: A young Bangladeshi tells of his unbearable life from a Russian war camp in Ukraine
summary_en: An unnamed young Bangladeshi recounts, in the first person, how a broker who first promised a North Macedonia visa sent him to Russia in 2024 for BDT 8 lakh; after a Chinese company in Blagoveshchensk stopped paying and expelled about 20 workers in February 2025, he was picked up at a Moscow airport by a stranger, made to sign an untranslated contract and sold to the Russian army. After a few days of weapons training from 20 March he was sent to Ukraine and, on his 29th day in war camps, is in Donetsk with no way to escape.

facts.statement: A broker first took the young man's passport promising a North Macedonia visa with work; in 2024 the broker said the Macedonia visa would not happen and instead offered a work visa at a 'good company' in Russia with a high salary.
facts.source_in_article: The unnamed Bangladeshi youth (first-person account as told to Shahadat Hossain)

facts.statement: The broker's stated cost for the Russia work visa was BDT 8 lakh, which the youth's family agreed to.
The promised monthly salary in Russia was 40-45 thousand roubles (stated as BDT 60-70 thousand).

About a month and a half after arriving in Russia he was sent to work in Blagoveshchensk, on the Chinese border. He had been sent for welding work but was made an electrician at a Chinese company named Sinopec (সিনোপ্যাক). After about two months pay became irregular, and in early February the company handed back passports and threw out him and about 20 others: two Nepalis, two Indians and the rest Bangladeshis.

The dismissed workers travelled 7,500 km from Blagoveshchensk to Moscow and split up. His group of five spent five days in a hotel, then tried to go home and went to the airport, living for 20 days at or near the airport on a little money, unable to communicate for lack of the language.

At the Moscow airport a man heard their story through Google Translate, said their visas were still valid and offered work, took them to a hotel and took their passports and all papers. Three or four Russians came and had them sign a contract they could not read, refusing them the chance to photograph and translate it and saying it was a work contract.

Promised meat-cutting work, the five were taken to a town far from Moscow and made to clear snow for about a week; then four people including a woman took them to a forest 'to cut trees' for four or five days, where guns and ammunition and soldiers in civilian clothes arrived and those who had brought them slipped away. They realised they had been sold.
When the five begged the Russian commander to release them, he referred to the contract and asked why they had signed it; told that they had not known what it was, he said nothing could now be done.

From 20 March the men received five days of training in loading and firing guns; on the sixth day they were sent to a Russian war camp in Ukraine, where he was separated from the other Bangladeshis and given two more days of training before being sent on an operation on the last day of March.

On his first operation a missile struck where the vehicles were parked and he survived because he was not in the vehicle. On 7 or 8 April he was sent on another operation from Luhansk deeper into Ukraine: 12 went and 6 came back. Recently ('the other day') a shell also hit his vehicle convoy and he narrowly got back alive. He has also heard of the death of another Bangladeshi in the camps.

On his 29th day in war camps he was in Russian-controlled Donetsk in his fifth camp, with 30-40 Russian soldiers; as the youngest he is mostly kept in camp carrying weapons, ammunition and food. Several other Bangladeshis are in different war camps and he is secretly in touch with many of them.

The men are not allowed to speak to their families; he calls secretly from beside or inside the toilet and is beaten if seen. In camp the food is dry bread and pasta at noon and night, and on operations they go without food. He says there is no chance to escape.
The Russian commander told him that if the Bangladesh government makes contact about his case, it would be possible to take him out of the camp.
facts.source_in_article: The Russian commander, as quoted by the youth

facts.statement: The article's introduction says quite a number of young Bangladeshis like him are now fighting in Ukraine for the Russian forces.

headline_en: Why the EU considers Bangladesh and Egypt 'safe' countries
summary_en: Based on a Euronews piece of 17 April 2025, the article explains the European Commission's proposed list of seven 'safe countries of origin' (Bangladesh, Egypt, Kosovo, Colombia, India, Morocco, Tunisia), published 16 April 2025, which if adopted will make asylum harder for their nationals. It gives the Commission's reasoning on Bangladesh and Egypt and asylum statistics: 4 percent recognition for both in 2024, and 33,455 Bangladeshi applicants in Italy.

facts.statement: The European Union published a list of seven countries it currently considers 'safe': Bangladesh, Egypt, Kosovo, Colombia, India, Morocco and Tunisia. If the relevant EU authorities pass the list, it will be harder for nationals of these countries to get asylum in EU member states.
facts.source_in_article: European Commission, via Euronews (Simone De La Feld)

facts.statement: Finalisation of the proposed EU safe-country list is awaiting an EU court order, according to the article.

The EU's guidance was that countries whose nationals file a significant number of asylum applications in the EU but have an approval rate of 5 percent or less can be called safe; the Commission also considered countries already on member states' own lists. Egypt and Bangladesh were on the lists of six EU member states.

In 2024, 4 percent of asylum applications from both Bangladeshi and Egyptian applicants were granted in the EU. About 68,000 applications were 'accepted/received' (গৃহীত, as printed) across the EU, 7 percent of them from Bangladeshis and Egyptians, and more than two-thirds of these applied in Italy.
facts.source_in_article: European Commission / EUAA data, via Euronews

facts.statement: In Italy in 2024, 21 percent of asylum applicants, 33,455 people, were Bangladeshi; Egyptians were 8 percent, 11,979 people. About 30 percent of asylum applications in Italy come from Bangladeshis and Egyptians.

Bangladesh and Egypt are among the countries whose asylum seekers Italy wants to send to Albania under its controversial fast-track processing plan; Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni said on 16 April that the Commission's list showed 'the data prove we were right'.

The Commission's assessment of Bangladesh: it is going through a political transition away from a repressive system; there is no armed conflict and so no threat of indiscriminate violence; there is no indication of Bangladeshi nationals being expelled or extradited to countries where they risk the death penalty, torture or inhuman treatment. It also notes occasional tensions with ethnic and religious minorities, discrimination against LGBTIQ people, criminalised homosexuality, widespread gender-based violence, reports of torture of detainees at least until the last government, and a death penalty that is rarely carried out.

The EU's conclusion: in light of the analysis and the low rate of accepted applications in the EU, the people of Bangladesh and Egypt are generally not subject to persecution or at risk of serious harm.

headline_en: What Pratik Group chairman Faruqi Hasan said about the 'BDT 730 crore' remittance
summary_en: After the NBR chairman said on 17 March 2025 that one businessman had brought BDT 730 crore into Bangladesh as remittance, Pratik Group chairman Syed Mohammad Faruqi Hasan told Prothom Alo the money was legitimate agent and consultancy fees earned over 13 years from Chinese state shipbuilders that sold 15 ships to the Bangladesh Navy. He said it came through an Eastern Bank account, was declared in his tax file with NBR certificates, and that he did not take the cash incentive.

facts.statement: NBR chairman Abdur Rahman Khan told journalists that one businessman had brought BDT 730 crore into the country as remittance (expatriate income), setting off wide discussion; journalists identified him the next day as Pratik Group chairman Syed Mohammad Faruqi Hasan.
facts.source_in_article: Abdur Rahman Khan, NBR chairman; reporter

facts.statement: Syed Mohammad Faruqi Hasan said he acts as agent and consultant for Chinese state shipbuilders, that the Bangladesh Navy bought 15 ships from them between 2011 and 2024, and that over 13 years he received agent and consultancy fees equivalent to BDT 730 crore, paid tax on it in China and brought it to Bangladesh as remittance in the name of Pratik Trade International through an Eastern Bank account, in stages over several years.

Faruqi Hasan said he was entitled to the cash incentive paid against remittances but did not take it, that he showed the money in his income-tax file, and that NBR gave him a certificate each year he brought money in. He has hired a lawyer to speak to NBR now that it is questioning the matter.

Faruqi Hasan, from Lakshmipur, moved to Canada in 2001, later returned to start businesses (Pratik Ceramic, Pratik Developer, Hotel Lake Castle and others), lives in both Bangladesh and Canada, was founding president of Ontario Awami League (no post now), and is a sponsor director of Bengal Commercial Bank. He says he built four factories employing about 3,000 people with the money.

headline_en: Trade among SAARC countries: who gains more, Bangladesh or India?
summary_en: A Bangladesh Bank report based on FY2023-24 data shows Bangladesh's trade with SAARC countries is small and dominated by India. On migration, it notes that few Bangladeshi workers go to South Asian countries: of USD 23.91 billion in remittances in FY2023-24 only USD 82.9 million came from SAARC countries, about 69 percent of that from the Maldives and about 23 percent from India.

facts.statement: Bangladesh received a total of USD 23.91 billion (2,391 crore dollars) in remittances in fiscal year 2023-24, of which USD 82.9 million (8 crore 29 lakh dollars), less than 1 percent, came from SAARC countries, because Bangladeshi workers do not go much to South Asian countries.
Among SAARC countries the largest source of remittances to Bangladesh is the Maldives, accounting for about 69 percent of remittances from SAARC countries; India accounts for about 23 percent.

Bangladesh exported USD 1,743.8 million of goods to SAARC countries (4.47 percent of its exports) and imported USD 9,762.5 million from them (15.44 percent of its imports); about 90 percent of those exports and 92.19 percent of those imports were with India.
Of about USD 1.47 billion in FDI into Bangladesh in fiscal year 2023-24, about USD 240 million (16.2 percent) came from SAARC countries.

headline_en: Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030: Bangladesh's business and investment prospects
summary_en: The Bangladesh Consulate General in Jeddah held a seminar on 26 February 2025 on trade, Saudi investment, export of trained and skilled manpower and sending remittances through banking channels. Expatriate leaders set out a list of budget demands (pension and health insurance for returnees, legal aid, budget for repatriating bodies, free trade training, help desks at police stations), and ambassador Mohammad Delwar Hossain said bringing skilled workers is the number one manpower priority.

facts.statement: The Bangladesh Consulate General, Jeddah held a seminar at a Jeddah hotel on bilateral trade, attracting Saudi investment, exporting trained and skilled manpower from Bangladesh and sending remittances through legal banking channels; Consul General Mia Md. Mainul Kabir chaired, Commercial Counsellor Syeda Nahida Habiba moderated, and ambassador Mohammad Delwar Hossain was chief guest.

Bangladesh's ambassador to Saudi Arabia Mohammad Delwar Hossain said the mission's target is to bring skilled people to Saudi Arabia, calling it the number one priority in manpower, and said that from talks in various parts of Saudi Arabia they learned that (the lack of) skilled professionals is an important obstacle.
facts.source_in_article: Mohammad Delwar Hossain, ambassador of Bangladesh to Saudi Arabia

facts.statement: The ambassador said he found many highly educated Bangladeshis, including engineers and doctors, working in important positions in Saudi Arabia, and cited community leaders' figure that five thousand Bangladeshi businesspeople are already registered there.
facts.source_in_article: Mohammad Delwar Hossain, citing community leaders

facts.statement: Expatriates' budget demands raised at the Jeddah seminar included: a special pension scheme and health insurance for returnee workers; expatriate housing estates; duty-free purchase of construction materials for building a home; budget for legal aid to workers dismissed or injured abroad; a separate EPZ for expatriates; quotas and scholarships for expatriates' children; income-tax exemption on expatriates' retirement savings; and Open University branches abroad.
facts.source_in_article: Expatriate community leaders at the seminar

facts.statement: Further demands: that no migrant worker be harassed when renewing a passport at missions abroad; a government budget allocation for sending home the bodies of migrants who die abroad; free, internationally accepted trade-based training and certification for prospective migrant workers; employment and skill-test-based overseas recruitment in which employers or agencies select workers on skill; and an expatriate help desk at every police station to protect migrants' property.
facts.source_in_article: Expatriate community leaders at the seminar

named_actors.name: Mohammad Delwar Hossain
named_actors.what_the_article_says: Bangladesh's ambassador to Saudi Arabia; said bringing skilled workers is the top manpower priority.

key_quote_bn: আমরা এখন স্কিল লোক এখানে আনতে চাই। এটা হলো আমাদের ম্যানপাওয়ারের ক্ষেত্রে নম্বর ১ প্রায়োরিটি
